title: Anabelian geometry
summary: This library studies how the geometry of a curve constrains its étale fundamental group, proving centralizer rigidity for hyperbolic curves and computing the genus-zero case with two punctures.
overview: For curves over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero, these results connect geometric features with the structure of the étale fundamental group. A proper curve of genus at least two, or a punctured curve satisfying the hyperbolicity inequality, has a slim fundamental group: every open subgroup has trivial centralizer in the whole group. This controls centralizing symmetries throughout its finite covering theory.

A genus-zero curve with two punctures gives the boundary case, where the fundamental group is the profinite completion of the integers and admits a topological generator. The present results establish these geometric properties; arithmetic reconstruction of curves and the corresponding positive-characteristic results remain outside their scope.
scopeNote: These selected theorems concern geometric curves over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero. They do not prove the Grothendieck conjecture, arithmetic reconstruction of curves from Galois-augmented groups, or the corresponding statements in positive characteristic. The project remains under development.

entries.title: Slimness for proper hyperbolic curves
entries.summary: Every open subgroup of the geometric fundamental group of a proper curve of genus at least two has trivial centralizer.

This is the library's predicate $\mathrm{IsSlim}(G)$. It quantifies over all open subgroups, including nonnormal ones.
discussion: This property, called slimness, controls centralizing symmetries throughout the finite covering theory of the curve. Centralizers also measure ambiguities when fundamental-group maps are considered up to inner automorphism. In the covering framework of SGA 1, it forms part of the setting for anabelian geometry; Mochizuki's 1999 work proves arithmetic reconstruction results over sub-p-adic fields, whereas the theorem here concerns geometric curves over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero.
history: SGA 1 made finite étale covers the foundation of the algebraic fundamental group. Grothendieck's anabelian perspective asks how much geometry such groups retain. Mochizuki's 1999 paper proves reconstruction results for hyperbolic curves over sub-p-adic fields; the geometric slimness theorem here is a structural result in that broader setting, rather than an arithmetic reconstruction theorem.

discussion: Punctures can provide the same centralizer rigidity as genus: a projective line with at least three punctures is already hyperbolic. Slimness controls finite covers as well as the curve itself. Such curves are central to the anabelian program built on SGA 1's covering theory; Mochizuki's 1999 work studies their arithmetic fundamental groups over sub-p-adic fields, while this result concerns the geometric group in characteristic zero.
history: SGA 1 supplies the finite-étale covering framework. Hyperbolic curves, including punctured curves, are central to Grothendieck's anabelian program. Mochizuki's 1999 work studies their arithmetic fundamental groups and pro-p variants over sub-p-adic fields. The geometric theorem on this page concerns a different, foundational question: centralizers inside the full fundamental group over an algebraically closed field.

entries.title: A genus-zero curve with two punctures
entries.summary: The actual étale fundamental group is the full profinite completion of the integers, with a chosen topological generator supplied by the conclusion.

discussion: A single topological generator accounts for the covering theory, as it does for the multiplicative group. This is the boundary before the hyperbolic genus-zero case reached by adding a third puncture. Classically, power maps on the multiplicative group lead to the profinite-integer description; SGA 1's theory of finite étale covers lets the calculation be transported to a genus-zero curve without choosing coordinates in advance.
history: The classical power maps on the multiplicative group lead to the profinite-integer description of its fundamental group in characteristic zero. SGA 1 places this calculation in the general theory of finite étale covers, which allows it to be transported to a genus-zero curve without choosing coordinates in advance.
